data: First mission to the Jupiter Trojans
The Lucy Spacecraft — NASA (16 m tip to tip, arrays deployed)
Levison et al. (2021) — Lucy Mission to the Trojan Asteroids (Space Science Reviews)

NASA's 12-year multi-flyby mission to 6 Jupiter Trojan asteroid systems and 2 main-belt asteroids (11 total encounters including satellites). Three Earth gravity assists shape a single trajectory visiting both the L4 and L5 Trojan clouds. Named for the 1974 Australopithecus afarensis fossil, in turn named for the Beatles song — the implication being that Trojans preserve early-solar-system material the way the fossil preserves early-human history.
First mission to the Jupiter Trojans; visits 11 bodies across 8 asteroids and their satellites in a single 12-year trajectory — a record number of objects on separate solar orbits
First mission to a metal-rich M-class asteroid
First mission dedicated to characterising Europa's habitability
Closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown
Sample-returned Bennu (2023); now en route to Apophis
Mars atmospheric loss to solar wind
